title: Big fppf to Zariski ringed comparison for arbitrary modules
statement: Fix universes and small presentations of sites as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ be its site of open subschemes with open coverings [def-sc-zariski-site], and let $\mathcal C_S=(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ be its big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site], with ring sheaf $\mathcal O(u:T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. There is a morphism of ringed topoi $\epsilon_S:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C_S),\mathcal O)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{Zar}}),\mathcal O_S)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] whose direct image on sheaves and on module sheaves is restriction to open subschemes; its structural ring map is adjoint to the identity $\mathcal O_S=\epsilon_{S,*}\mathcal O$. For every Zariski $\mathcal O_S$-module $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], without any quasi-coherence hypothesis, the tensor pullback $L_SM=\mathcal O\otimes_{\epsilon_S^{-1}\mathcal O_S}\epsilon_S^{-1}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is canonically the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $P_M(u:T\to S)=\Gamma(T,u^*M)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Here restriction along $h:T'\to T$ is pullback of sections followed by $h^*u^*M\simeq(uh)^*M$, and $P_v(u)=\Gamma(T,u^*v)$ for every module map $v:M\to N$. The comparison is natural in $M$ and respects these restrictions and scalar actions. For each open $j:W\hookrightarrow S$, the component $M(W)\to(L_SM)(W)$ of the adjunction unit is $P_M(j)\to P_M^\#(j)$ under $P_M(j)=M(W)$ and $L_SM=P_M^\#$.

source.place: Tag 070R (remark-change-topologies-ringed): ringed structure on the big-to-small morphism; Tag 070S (lemma-compare-sites), part (1), with tau = fppf, and its proof: tensor pullback is the sheafification of the section presheaf. The last unit equation specifies the canonical comparison used in that proof.

proof.text: First check the stipulated structure ring. On every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$, the rank-one case of the tilde/free-module theorem gives $\mathcal O_S|_W\simeq\widetilde A$; thus $\mathcal O_S$ is quasi-coherent by the affine-local definition. For any $u:T\to S$, the unit-normalized isomorphism $u^*\mathcal O_S\simeq\mathcal O_T$ identifies pullback of its sections with the usual ring restriction. Every fppf covering is fpqc, and fpqc descent of sections, applied only to $\mathcal O_S$, therefore says that $T\mapsto\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ is an fppf sheaf. Its ring operations commute with restrictions, so it is the ring sheaf $\mathcal O$ used below. This argument puts no quasi-coherence condition on $M$.

source.place: Tags 03DT (lemma-sheaf-condition-holds) and 03DU (definition-structure-sheaf); structure module is the rank-one affine tilde module

proof.text: Let $i:S_{\mathrm{Zar}}\to\mathcal C_S$ send $W$ to $W\hookrightarrow S$. The terminal object is sent to $S\xrightarrow{1}S$. A fibre product of open inclusions is their intersection: a map to both opens over a third factors uniquely through the intersection. The open-preimage fibre-product lemma identifies that intersection with the scheme fibre product, so $i$ preserves finite limits. Zariski covers become fppf covers by the cited covering lemma. The finite-limit/cover-preserving site theorem now supplies a geometric adjunction $\epsilon^{-1}\dashv R$, with $R(G)(W)=G(W\hookrightarrow S)$. All sites and Kan indices are small in the chosen larger universe. Since $R\mathcal O=\mathcal O_S$ sectionwise as rings, apply the continuous ringed-topos construction to the identity ring map $\mathcal O_S\to R\mathcal O$. It gives $\epsilon_S$ with the asserted structural map and with module direct image exactly restriction, including its scalar action.

source.place: Tag 070R (remark-change-topologies-ringed), identity scheme map and inclusion of Zariski opens; sites.tex Tag 00X6 via the cited site theorem

proof.text:
We fix the canonical pullback comparisons precisely. Write $\eta^u:M\to u_*u^*M$ for the scheme-module adjunction unit. Direct images compose sectionwise. Thus $h^*u^*$ and $(uh)^*$ are left adjoint to the same functor $u_*h_*=(uh)_*$. The composite-adjunction formula and uniqueness of left adjoints give the natural isomorphism $c_{h,u}:h^*u^*\xrightarrow{\sim}(uh)^*$ characterized by
$$(uh)_*(c_{h,u,M})\,u_*(\eta^h_{u^*M})\,\eta^u_M=\eta^{uh}_M.$$
The identity comparison is normalized in the same way. Module direct images along composable scheme maps are equal as functors, $(uhk)_*=u_*h_*k_*$, so the associativity lemma for unit-normalized composition isomorphisms of left adjoints applies to $u,h,k$: $c_{hk,u}\circ c_{k,h,u^*M}=c_{k,uh}\circ k^*(c_{h,u})$ as maps $k^*h^*u^*M\to(uhk)^*M$. For an open $k:A\hookrightarrow T$, use the unit-compatible comparison $\kappa_k:N|_A\simeq k^*N$. These choices identify $(u|_A)^*M$ with $(u^*M)|_A$ compatibly with restriction and units.

source.place: Tags 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules), and 00A0 (lemma-j-pullback); canonical comparisons normalized by their units

proof.text: Define $P_M(u)=\Gamma(T,u^*M)$ and $\rho_h(s)=\Gamma(c_{h,u})(\eta^h_{u^*M}(s))$ for $h:T'\to T$. The unit is additive and semilinear, and $c_{h,u}$ is linear, so $\rho_h(as)=h^\sharp(a)\rho_h(s)$. The unit equation in step 3 gives $\rho_1=1$ and $\rho_{hk}=\rho_k\rho_h$: both are the unit for the full composite followed by the same normalized comparison. Naturality of $\eta$ and $c$ gives $\rho_h^N\Gamma(T,u^*v)=\Gamma(T',(uh)^*v)\rho_h^M$ for every $v:M\to N$. Since pullback is a functor, the resulting $P_v$ preserve identity maps and composition. Thus these formulas define a functor from Zariski modules to presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. On an open $j:W\hookrightarrow S$, $\Gamma(\kappa_j)$ identifies $M(W)$ with $P_M(j)$; the unit compatibility in step 3 makes restrictions between opens the original restrictions of $M$.

source.place: Tag 070S (lemma-compare-sites)(1), its section presheaf; direct verification using the scheme-module unit

proof.text:
For a big-site module sheaf $G$ and $u:T\to S$, put $G_u(A)=G(A\hookrightarrow T\xrightarrow{u}S)$ on Zariski opens $A$ of $T$. This is an $\mathcal O_T$-module sheaf because every open cover of $A$ is an fppf cover. For $\beta:M\to RG$ define a module map $b_u:M\to u_*G_u$ by
$$b_{u,W}(m)=G(u^{-1}W\to W)(\beta_W(m)).$$
Its scalar linearity and commutation with open restriction are the module-presheaf axioms for $G$ and $\beta$. By the scheme-module adjunction there is a unique $a_u:u^*M\to G_u$ with $u_*a_u\circ\eta^u_M=b_u$. Set $\Theta(\beta)_u=\Gamma(T,a_u)$.

source.place: Tag 0096 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); construction of the maps used to verify descent.tex Tag 070S(1)

proof.text:
Check all arrows, rather than only open arrows. For $h:T'\to T$ the restrictions of $G$ give $\gamma_h:G_u\to h_*G_{uh}$, whose component on $A\subseteq T$ is $G(h^{-1}A\to A)$. Let $d_h:h^*G_u\to G_{uh}$ be its adjoint. Compare the two maps from $h^*u^*M$ to $G_{uh}$:
$$a_{uh}c_{h,u}\quad\hbox{and}\quad d_hh^*a_u.$$
Under the composite adjunction of step 3 their transposes are respectively $b_{uh}$ and $u_*\gamma_h\circ b_u$. On $W\subseteq S$, both send $m$ to $G((uh)^{-1}W\to W)(\beta_W(m))$, since restriction in $G$ composes. Injectivity of that Hom bijection proves their equality. Finally $h_*d_h\circ\eta^h=\gamma_h$ says on global sections that $\Theta(\beta)_{uh}\rho_h=G(h)\Theta(\beta)_u$. Thus $\Theta(\beta)$ is a morphism of module presheaves on the whole big site, with its given scalar actions.

source.place: Tag 0096 and lemma-push-pull-composition-modules: equality of adjuncts using the composite unit; explicit argument for descent.tex Tag 070S(1)

proof.text:
Conversely, let $\theta:P_M\to G$ be a morphism of module presheaves. On opens set $\beta_W=\theta_j\Gamma(\kappa_j)$ for $j:W\hookrightarrow S$; step 4 shows that this is a module-sheaf map $M\to RG$. For fixed $u:T\to S$, the components $\theta_{u|_A}$ for all opens $A\subseteq T$, through the identifications of step 3, form an $\mathcal O_T$-linear sheaf map $a^\theta_u:u^*M\to G_u$. To compute its adjoint on $W\subseteq S$, evaluate it on $\eta^u(m)$ over $u^{-1}W$. The unit equation of step 3 identifies this section with pullback of $\kappa_j(m)$ along $u^{-1}W\to W$. Naturality of $\theta$ for precisely that big-site arrow gives
$$u_*a^\theta_u(\eta^u(m))=G(u^{-1}W\to W)(\beta_W(m))=b_{u,W}(m).$$
Hence $a^\theta_u=a_u$ by the scheme-module adjunction, and $\theta=\Theta(\beta)$. For the other composite, take $u=j$ open: $u^{-1}W$ is an intersection and the open-pullback unit is restriction, so the defining equation of $a_j$ gives $\Theta(\beta)_j\Gamma(\kappa_j)=\beta_W$. The two assignments are therefore inverse.

source.place: Tag 0096 and Tag 00A0, unit-compatible restriction to open subsets; uniqueness part of the explicit adjunction for descent.tex Tag 070S(1)

proof.text:
These inverse bijections are natural in both variables. If $v:M'\to M$ and $k:G\to G'$ are module maps, the formula for $b_u$ gives $b'_u=(u_*k_u)b_uv$ for the input $R(k)\beta v$. Naturality of the scheme-module Hom bijection gives $a'_u=k_ua_uu^*v$, and therefore $\Theta(R(k)\beta v)=k\Theta(\beta)P_v$ on each object. Apply module sheafification: its universal property gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P_M^\#,G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O)}(P_M,G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_S}(M,RG).$$
Thus $B(M)=P_M^\#$, with the stated maps, is left adjoint to the actual restriction functor $R$.

The ringed-topos module-adjunction theorem applied to $\epsilon_S$ of step 2 says that $L_SM=\mathcal O\otimes_{\epsilon_S^{-1}\mathcal O_S}\epsilon_S^{-1}M$ is also left adjoint to the same module restriction $R$. Apply the uniqueness theorem with the identity comparison of right adjoints to obtain a unique natural isomorphism $e:L_S\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ carrying the tensor-pullback unit to the unit of $B\dashv R$. Its components are isomorphisms of module sheaves, so they commute with every big-site restriction and scalar action, and its naturality identifies $L_S(v)$ with the sheafification of $P_v$. This proves the asserted canonical comparison, without assuming $P_M$ itself is an fppf sheaf.

source.place: Tag 070S (lemma-compare-sites)(1); module adjunction in sites-modules.tex Tag 03D3, and categories.tex Tag 0B65 via the cited uniqueness theorem

proof.text: Write $q_M:P_M\to P_M^\#$ for the sheafification map. The unit of $B\dashv R$ is obtained by sending $1_{B(M)}$ through the two Hom bijections of step 8. The first gives $q_M$; the second restricts it to opens and composes with $\Gamma(\kappa_j)$. Hence on $j:W\hookrightarrow S$ that unit is $q_M(j)\Gamma(\kappa_j):M(W)\to P_M^\#(j)$. Since $e$ carries units to units, $e_M(j)\eta_{L,M}(W)$ is this same map. Under $P_M(j)=M(W)$ and $L_SM\simeq P_M^\#$, this is exactly the last equation in the statement. The formula also proves its compatibility with restrictions in $W$ and with module maps, because $q_M$ and $\kappa_j$ are natural.
